Architecture Diagram

The repository contains a public job-search web application and a separate console utility for loading sample data. Both use Azure AI Search indexes as their shared data boundary.

Data Storage & External Services

Azure AI Search stores job postings and postal-code location records in the nycjobs and zipcodes indexes. The web application reads those indexes, while DataLoader reads repository JSON/schema files and sends index-management and document-upload requests. No relational database, message broker, or cache is configured.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The web application and data loader are separate projects that share Azure Search indexes rather than a relational database.
  • Job search, suggestions, and document lookup are handled by one MVC controller and a dedicated search wrapper.
  • Sample records and index schemas are repository files used by the standalone loader.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob is the mutable JSON response envelope for search results, facets, and count. NYCJobLookup wraps a single Azure Search SearchDocument for job details. The application uses Azure Search SDK models for individual records; no dedicated immutable request/response records, OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema was found. JSON serialization is provided by ASP.NET MVC and the Azure SDK.

Communication Patterns

  • The browser posts search input to the MVC application and receives JSON results; it requests suggestions and job details through the MVC actions.
  • JobsSearch calls Azure AI Search synchronously for search, suggestions, postal-code lookup, and document lookup.
  • DataLoader uses synchronous HttpClient calls to the Azure Search REST API to create indexes and upload documents from local files.
  • No message broker, asynchronous event flow, service discovery, API gateway, retry policy, circuit breaker, or explicit timeout policy was identified.
  • No application-level authentication, authorization, or HTTPS enforcement is configured. DataLoader targets Azure Search over HTTPS; the web application's hosting transport is not specified.

Core Business Workflows

The application helps users search publicly sourced New York City job postings by text, title, posting type, salary, and location. A separate utility loads sample job postings and postal-code records into Azure AI Search.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
JobPostingNYCJobsWeb / Job SearchA public listing with role, agency, salary, location, and descriptionAssociated with a geographic point; searchable by facets
PostalCodeNYCJobsWeb / Location SearchA postal-code lookup entry with locality and coordinatesSupplies a point used for distance-based job filtering

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob SearchReads JobPosting and PostalCode index documentsAzure AI Search
DataLoaderSearch Data ImportCreates and populates the job and postal-code indexesAzure AI Search and repository sample data

Azure AI Search is the source of truth for the indexed records. DataLoader imports checked-in sample records; the web application does not mutate the index.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search job postings

  1. The browser submits search text, selected facets, sort option, page, and map/location values to Home/Search.
  2. Blank search text is treated as a wildcard search. If a maximum distance is selected, the application first queries the postal-code index for coordinates.
  3. JobsSearch builds Azure Search text, facet, sort, and optional spatial filter parameters.
  4. Azure AI Search returns job documents, facets, and a total count; the MVC action returns the data as JSON for the page to display.

Workflow 2: View job details

  1. The browser submits a job document ID to Home/LookUp.
  2. JobsSearch retrieves the document from the job index.
  3. The action returns a JSON wrapper, and the detail page displays the selected job fields.

Workflow 3: Load sample indexes

  1. An operator runs DataLoader with Azure Search service credentials configured in App.config.
  2. The utility deletes each target index if present, creates the index from its checked-in schema, and uploads matching JSON files.
  3. The new indexes are then available to the web application's search and location lookups.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The web application and loader communicate through the Azure Search indexes, not direct process calls or a message broker. The loader owns index creation and sample-data upload; the web application reads jobs and postal-code records. The spatial search flow uses a postal-code result to derive coordinates and then applies a distance constraint to the job search. No downstream-service fallback or circuit breaker was identified.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User as "Job seeker" participant Web as "NYCJobsWeb" participant Search as "JobsSearch" participant Zip as "Postal code index" participant Jobs as "Job index" User->>Web: Submit job search and optional location Web->>Web: Replace blank search text with wildcard alt Distance filter selected Web->>Search: Resolve postal code coordinates Search->>Zip: Search postal-code index Zip-->>Search: Location coordinates Search-->>Web: Coordinates else No distance filter Note over Web: Use the submitted map center end Web->>Search: Search text, facets, sort, and location Search->>Jobs: Query jobs index Jobs-->>Search: Job documents, facets, and count Search-->>Web: Search results Web-->>User: JSON results for display

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Empty search text is converted to * so users receive an unrestricted text search.
  • A positive maximum distance triggers postal-code coordinate lookup and a spatial distance filter.
  • Supported sort choices include featured, salary ascending/descending, and most recent.
  • Job title, posting type, and salary facets are combined when supplied.
  • DataLoader replaces its target indexes before importing sample data; no transaction or rollback behavior is implemented.
  • No business-level authentication or authorization rule was identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The projects target .NET Framework 4.7.2 and 4.5 and use older ASP.NET MVC and NuGet packages. The dependency assessment found vulnerable versions of Newtonsoft.Json, Microsoft.Rest.ClientRuntime, System.Text.Encodings.Web, and jQuery; see the security assessment for affected ranges and advisories.

Notable Observations

  • The projects declare different Newtonsoft.Json versions: 10.0.3 for the web application and 9.0.1 for DataLoader.
  • dotnet list package --include-transitive could not resolve the legacy projects on this host, so this inventory reflects declared packages only; transitive packages are not available from a lock file.
  • The web application declares both Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json dependencies.
  • No test-scoped dependencies are declared.

Entity Model

The application uses Azure Search SearchDocument objects rather than mapped ORM entities. Index field definitions are stored in NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data/*.schema; the documents contain job-posting data and postal-code/geolocation data. No entity relationships, transactions, or repository interfaces were identified.

Caching Strategy

No application cache, distributed cache, or explicit query-result cache was identified. Search clients are held in static fields in the web application; this is client reuse, not a result cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

Both projects use the same Azure AI Search service and its two indexes. The web application is read-oriented; DataLoader is a separate import utility that creates indexes, deletes existing indexes, and uploads sample data. No cross-service database access, CQRS pattern, or shared relational database was identified.
